response.title: What dehumidifier works in an unheated garage or basement that gets down to 45 degrees in winter without icing up?
response.answer:
For an unheated garage or basement that drops to 45°F (7°C) in winter, you want a dehumidifier specifically rated for low-temperature operation.

The key distinction is that a dehumidifier with automatic defrost is not necessarily one that works well at 45°F. Many ordinary household models can prevent permanent icing by periodically shutting off their compressors, but they remove very little moisture at that temperature.

There are two good options:

Desiccant dehumidifier — best for avoiding ice. These don't rely on a cold evaporator coil, so they can operate in much colder conditions. They're especially suitable for winter use.

Low-temperature compressor dehumidifier — best for energy efficiency. Look for a manufacturer-specified operating range extending to at least 41°F (5°C), ideally lower, with automatic defrost.
